creative_strategies.description: Showing players making bad decisions or losing — triggers 'I can do better' response
Satisfying gameplay loops with sound effects (dice rolling, coins collecting)
Mini-storylines about rivalry, revenge, or rags-to-riches
Showing winners, big jackpots, and player testimonials
Leveraging the classic Monopoly brand nostalgia

inferred_targeting_strategy.primary_audience: Female 30-55, casual gamers, board game fans
inferred_targeting_strategy.retargeting: Users who played casual games, puzzle games, or casino-style games
inferred_targeting_strategy.lookalike: Based on high-value payers (whales spending $1000+). Uses 4-stage AI training pipeline: install farming → proxy events → purchase modeling → value optimization
inferred_targeting_strategy.geo_strategy: Separate AI models per region (US, Japan, Korea, Tier 3) to prevent model collapse

overall_assessment.strategy_focus: Monopoly Go! operates the most sophisticated ad strategy in mobile gaming. Their approach treats Meta's advertising platform as an AI training system rather than a media buying channel. They use 5 distinct creative formats (fail hooks, ASMR, narrative, social proof, brand) to segment users by psychological profile before they even install the game.
overall_assessment.competitive_position: Industry benchmark. $250-400M annual ad spend driving $1B+ revenue. The 'whale training' pipeline using CAPI (Conversions API) to feed real revenue data back to Meta's algorithm is considered the gold standard.
overall_assessment.key_innovation: Creative as user segmentation — each creative type acts as a latent selector for different user clusters (fail ads → casual moms, ASMR → hyper-casual, narrative → female midcore, social proof → whales)
